subject: general
question: Which of the following is India's longest railway tunnel?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pir Panjal Railway Tunnel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Pir Panjal Railway Tunnel, also known as the Banihal-Qazigund Tunnel, is the longest railway tunnel in India.
 
• It is located in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir and is part of the Jammu-Baramulla line.
 
• The tunnel is approximately 11.2 kilometers (7 miles) long.
 
• The construction of the tunnel was completed in June 2013, and it was inaugurated by then Prime Minister Manmohan Singh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geographical Significance:**

 
 
• The tunnel passes through the Pir Panjal Range of the Himalayas, a significant geographical feature in Northern India.
 
 
 
• **Engineering Feat:**
 
 
• The construction required advanced tunneling techniques due to the difficult and challenging terrain.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• This tunnel significantly reduces the travel time between Banihal and Qazigund, boosting trade and connectivity in the region.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Measures:**
 
 
• Special care was taken to minimize the environmental impact during the construction of the tunnel.
